problem: Public routes could inherit different historical shell dimensions, allowing header, navigation, footer and mega-menu geometry to drift by route.
root_cause: Multiple generations of site chrome retained different width and height values while the live V18 shell had become the effective production authority.
fix: Make the V18 production chrome the single geometry authority, load its canonical dimensions in head before first layout, and enforce route-to-route browser parity.
failed_approaches: Keeping legacy 1120px component geometry alongside the live 1220px V18 shell.
Fixing individual routes with page-specific header, footer or menu overrides.
Testing mega-menu contrast and width without also asserting header, navigation and footer parity.
Injecting the canonical geometry stylesheet at the end of body; browser visibility testing exposed mobile CLS above the 0.100 contract.
prevention: Never add route-local geometry overrides for header, navigation, footer or mega-menu.
All new public routes inherit the canonical shell.
Representative routes are compared in browser regression checks.
A geometry contract change requires same-lineage skill, docs, learning and System Map updates.
Load canonical shell geometry in head before first layout to prevent mobile cumulative layout shift.
